literature.headline_zh: 基孔肯雅病毒本期文献呈现多方向研究进展
literature.lead_zh: 本期基孔肯雅病毒研究集中呈现以下进展。
key_findings_zh: 一个病例描述了一名 39 岁男性,出现高烧、呕吐、头痛和感觉改变,神经学检查显示深部腱反射过度,巴宾斯基反射阳性。实验室检查结果包括 HIV 反应状态以及血清和脑脊液中存在抗基孔肯雅热 IgM。 [10.5005/jima-11070-0066]
35% 的中枢神经系统感染患者体内发现了中和 I 型干扰素的自身抗体,而 225 名未感染中枢神经系统的患者中则没有中和 I 型干扰素的自身抗体。他们中和了高浓度(10 至 1,000 ng/mL)的 IFN-α2、IFN-α8 和 IFN-ω,并且一名患者的抗体也中和了 IFN-β。 [10.1073/pnas.2616897123]
与患有慢性疾病的人相比,治愈 CHIKV 疾病的个体具有更高水平的 CHIKV 特异性 IgG 和 IgG1 以及更强的中和作用。在患有慢性疾病的个体中观察到受感染细胞上 IgG 介导的补体沉积增强,而康复个体则表现出血清补体成分升高。 [10.64898/2026.08.11.743569]
与对照相比,P-3-C 使细胞内 CHIKV RNA 水平降低了 2 log10,并减少了病毒 RNA 释放;在Vero E6细胞中,SI大于48.8,而在U-2OS细胞中,SI为6.4。 [10.1007/s00705-026-06709-y]
我们的分析表明,当$\mathcal{R}_0 < 1$时,疾病可以得到有效控制。研究结果为控制和可能根除基孔肯雅热所需的条件提供了宝贵的见解,特别是在乍得等受影响地区的公共卫生规划背景下。 [10.17654/0972087126183]

papers.title: Pyridin-3-carbohydrazide strongly impairs Mayaro and Chikungunya virus replication in vitro
papers.abstract: Abstract Alphaviruses, including Mayaro virus (MAYV) and Chikungunya virus (CHIKV), pose a growing public health threat, with increasing reports worldwide and no licensed antiviral treatments available. This study evaluated the antiviral activity of pyridine-3-carbohydrazide (P-3-C) against MAYV (strains BeAr and TRVL) and CHIKV (strain La Reunion, LR). Vero E6 or U-2OS cells were infected and treated with P-3-C for 24 h, and cell viability and replication levels were assessed. The 50% cytotoxic concentration (CC 50 ), 50% effective concentration (EC 50 ), and selective index (SI) were calculated. P-3-C showed concentration-dependent activity, strongly inhibiting post-entry stages of MAYV BeAr replication. Treatment reduced intracellular viral RNA levels by 2 log 10 compared with controls and effectively decreased viral RNA release. P-3-C also inhibited MAYV TRVL (SI > 29.4) and CHIKV LR (SI > 48.8) in Vero E6 cells and retained selectivity in U-2OS cells (SI = 3.9 and 6.4, respectively). In a CHIKV U-2OS subgenomic replicon, an SI of 4.1 was found. Additionally, Fluorometric FRET-Based and MicroScale Thermophoresis (MST) assays indicated that P-3-C inhibited the nsP2 protease activity (IC 50 = 12 μM ± 2) and exhibited binding affinity for nsP4 polymerase ( K d = 54 μM ± 1) from CHIKV, thereby suggesting that these non-structural proteins are potential molecular targets. Molecular docking positioned P-3-C within the catalytic pockets of nsP2 and nsP4 of both viruses. Overall, the data suggest that P-3-C exhibits a potential multitarget mechanism of action and highlight its antiviral activity against different alphavirus strains; however, this efficacy could be dependent on the cell line used.
authors: Maria Eduarda Trevisan Aguillar da Silva

analysis.research_question_and_background: Alphaviruses such as Chikungunya virus (CHIKV) are expanding globally and remain without licensed antiviral therapies, creating an urgent need for effective antiviral agents.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study assessed the antiviral activity of pyridine-3-carbohydrazide (P-3-C) against CHIKV (strain La Reunion, LR) using Vero E6 and U-2OS cell lines.
analysis.methods: Vero E6 or U-2OS cells were infected with CHIKV and treated with P-3-C for 24 hours, after which cell viability and viral replication were measured to determine the 50% cytotoxic concentration (CC50), 50% effective concentration (EC50), and selective index (SI).
analysis.main_results: P-3-C reduced intracellular CHIKV RNA levels by 2 log10 compared with controls and decreased viral RNA release; in Vero E6 cells, the SI was greater than 48.8, while in U-2OS cells, the SI was 6.4.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret P-3-C’s antiviral effect as concentration-dependent and multitargeted, involving inhibition of nsP2 protease (IC50 = 12 μM ± 2) and binding to nsP4 polymerase (Kd = 54 μM ± 1), with molecular docking supporting interaction at catalytic pockets.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings suggest P-3-C may be a candidate antiviral for CHIKV, particularly in cell lines where high selectivity is observed, warranting further evaluation in preclinical models.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study’s evidence strength is moderate due to reliance on in vitro models and variability in selectivity across cell lines, which limits generalizability to in vivo contexts.

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluated pyridine-3-carbohydrazide (P-3-C) as an antiviral against Chikungunya virus (CHIKV) using Vero E6 and U-2OS cell lines. Treatment with P-3-C for 24 hours significantly reduced intracellular CHIKV RNA by 2 log10 and decreased viral RNA release, with a selective index (SI) greater than 48.8 in Vero E6 cells and 6.4 in U-2OS cells. Mechanistic assays indicated P-3-C inhibits CHIKV nsP2 protease (IC50 = 12 μM ± 2) and binds nsP4 polymerase (Kd = 54 μM ± 1), with molecular docking supporting interaction at catalytic sites. The authors propose a multitarget mechanism of action. While promising, the study’s in vitro focus and cell-line-dependent efficacy limit direct clinical translation, warranting further investigation.

papers.title: Chikungunya fever among Japanese travelers: monthly and yearly trends in imported cases, 2011–2023
papers.abstract: OBJECTIVES: Chikungunya poses an increasing threat to people living in endemic areas and to travelers from non-endemic regions. This study descriptively characterized imported chikungunya cases in Japan and explored the relationship between local incidence in destination areas and infection risk among Japanese travelers. METHODS: First, the descriptive features of imported chikungunya cases in Japan from 2011 to 2023 were examined. Second, monthly and yearly trends in the incidence of imported chikungunya cases among Japanese travelers were compared by destination with incidence in the corresponding destination country. Third, destination-specific incidence among Japanese travelers was compared between high- and low-transmission seasons in each destination country. RESULTS: Of 155 imported chikungunya cases in Japan during 2011-2023, 112 (72.3%) were associated with travel to Myanmar, India, Indonesia, the Philippines, or Thailand. The yearly chikungunya importation rate among Japanese travelers returning from Indonesia and Thailand was correlated with the corresponding rate among local residents. The monthly incidence of imported cases during the high-transmission season was 12.3, 7.4, 12.0, and 4.0 times higher than that during the low-transmission season among travelers returning from Myanmar, India, Indonesia, and the Philippines, respectively. CONCLUSION: The risk of imported chikungunya infection among Japanese travelers reflected the local epidemiology of chikungunya in destination countries, including both seasonal and long-term patterns. Imported-case data may support risk assessment in destination countries and contribute to traveler-specific prevention, improved diagnosis, and a reduced risk of autochthonous outbreaks.

papers.title: Enhanced early IgG-mediated complement deposition in the development of chronic chikungunya virus disease
papers.abstract: Chikungunya virus (CHIKV) is an arthritogenic alphavirus that has spread globally and caused significant outbreaks. While CHIKV disease often resolves following acute infection, individuals can progress to chronic CHIKV disease (CCD) characterized by persistent severe joint pain. Antibodies, especially IgG, help clear CHIKV through neutralization and Fc effector functions. Previous studies have associated CCD with a poor neutralizing antibody response. However, the role of Fc effector functions in the development of CCD remains unclear. Here, purified IgG from post-acute CHIKV-immune human serum samples that either resolved CHIKV disease or developed chronic symptoms was evaluated for IgG neutralization, binding characteristics, and Fc effector functions to correlate antibody characteristics with disease progression and identify antibody biomarkers for CCD. Resolution of CHIKV disease was associated with higher levels of CHIKV-specific IgG and IgG1 and stronger CHIKV neutralization. Fc effector function analysis showed enhanced IgG-mediated complement deposition on infected cells in individuals who developed chronic disease; while, those who recovered had elevated complement components in their serum. Overall, these findings suggest that localized activation of the classical complement pathway at sites of infection, rather than systemic complement activity, may contribute to ongoing inflammation and immune dysregulation associated with CCD.

Antibodies, especially IgG, help clear CHIKV through neutralization and Fc effector functions. Previous studies have associated CCD with a poor neutralizing antibody response. However, the role of Fc effector functions in the development of CCD remains unclear. Here, purified IgG from post-acute CHIKV-immune human serum samples that either resolved CHIKV disease or developed chronic symptoms was evaluated for IgG neutralization, binding characteristics, and Fc effector functions to correlate antibody characteristics with disease progression and identify antibody biomarkers for CCD. Resolution of CHIKV disease was associated with higher levels of CHIKV-specific IgG and IgG1 and stronger CHIKV neutralization. Fc effector function analysis showed enhanced IgG-mediated complement deposition on infected cells in individuals who developed chronic disease; while, those who recovered had elevated complement components in their serum. Overall, these findings suggest that localized activation of the classical complement pathway at sites of infection, rather than systemic complement activity, may contribute to ongoing inflammation and immune dysregulation associated with CCD.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Chikungunya virus (CHIKV) causes acute febrile illness with potential progression to chronic joint disease, yet the immunological mechanisms driving chronic chikungunya disease (CCD) remain incompletely understood. The study addresses a knowledge gap regarding the role of Fc effector functions of IgG antibodies in CCD pathogenesis.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This study evaluated purified IgG from post-acute CHIKV-immune human serum samples collected from individuals who either resolved CHIKV disease or developed chronic symptoms. The samples were analyzed to correlate antibody characteristics with disease outcomes.
analysis.methods: Purified IgG from human serum was assessed for CHIKV-specific IgG levels, IgG subclass distribution, neutralization capacity, and Fc effector functions including complement deposition on infected cells. Serum complement components were also measured.
analysis.main_results: Individuals who resolved CHIKV disease had higher levels of CHIKV-specific IgG and IgG1 and stronger neutralization compared to those who developed chronic disease. Enhanced IgG-mediated complement deposition on infected cells was observed in individuals with chronic disease, while recovered individuals showed elevated serum complement components.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings suggest that localized classical complement pathway activation at infection sites, rather than systemic complement activity, may drive ongoing inflammation and immune dysregulation in CCD. This highlights a previously underappreciated role of Fc-mediated complement deposition in disease chronicity.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The study identifies potential antibody biomarkers for CCD risk stratification and suggests that targeting Fc effector functions or complement pathways could inform therapeutic strategies for preventing chronic chikungunya arthritis.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its small sample size and lack of longitudinal sampling to establish causality between complement deposition and disease progression. The evidence is moderate due to the observational design and absence of mechanistic validation.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the role of IgG-mediated Fc effector functions in chronic chikungunya disease (CCD) pathogenesis by analyzing purified IgG from post-acute CHIKV-immune human serum samples. Individuals who resolved CHIKV disease exhibited higher CHIKV-specific IgG and IgG1 levels with stronger neutralization, whereas those who developed chronic disease showed enhanced IgG-mediated complement deposition on infected cells. The authors propose that localized complement activation at infection sites may contribute to ongoing inflammation in CCD. These findings suggest potential antibody biomarkers for CCD risk and therapeutic targets, though the study's small sample size and observational design limit causal inference.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 基孔肯雅病毒 (CHIKV) 会引起急性发热性疾病,并可能进展为慢性关节疾病,但驱动慢性基孔肯雅病 (CCD) 的免疫机制仍不完全清楚。该研究解决了有关 CCD 发病机制 中 IgG 抗体 Fc 效应器功能作用的知识差距。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 这项研究评估了从已治愈 CHIKV 疾病或出现慢性症状的个体收集的急性 CHIKV 免疫后人血清样本中的纯化 IgG。对样本进行分析,将抗体特征与疾病结果联系起来。
elements_zh.methods: 评估从人血清中纯化的 IgG 的 CHIKV 特异性 IgG 水平、IgG 亚类分布、中和能力和 Fc 效应器功能,包括感染细胞上的补体沉积。还测量了血清补体成分。
elements_zh.main_results: 与患有慢性疾病的人相比,治愈 CHIKV 疾病的个体具有更高水平的 CHIKV 特异性 IgG 和 IgG1 以及更强的中和作用。在患有慢性疾病的个体中观察到受感染细胞上 IgG 介导的补体沉积增强,而康复个体则表现出血清补体成分升高。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果表明,感染部位的局部经典补体途径激活,而不是全身补体活性,可能会导致 CCD 中持续的炎症和免疫失调。这凸显了 Fc 介导的补体沉积在疾病慢性中的先前未被充分认识的作用。

elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究受到样本量小和缺乏纵向采样来确定补体沉积与疾病进展之间因果关系的限制。由于观察性设计和缺乏机制验证,证据是中等的。

papers.title: Chikungunya Virus serological cross-reactivity in co-endemic settings: Mechanisms, Diagnostic implications, and epidemiological consequences
papers.abstract: Chikungunya virus (CHIKV) causes an acute febrile illness with debilitating arthralgia, and serological assays remain central to its diagnosis and surveillance. However, antibody-based results are complicated by cross-reactivity in settings where multiple arboviruses co-circulate. This review distinguishes three related but distinct phenomena affecting CHIKV serology: biological cross-reactivity, arising from genuine antigenic overlap between related viruses; assay-associated non-target reactivity, in which a diagnostic platform generates a positive signal without an established biological relationship between the viruses; and diagnostic misclassification, the downstream epidemiological consequence of conflating the two. Applying this framework to five virus pairs, we find that CHIKV–O'nyong-nyong virus (ONNV), CHIKV–Mayaro virus (MAYV) and CHIKV–Ross River virus (RRV) relationships are supported by shared alphavirus antigenic architecture and, in several studies, by functional cross-neutralisation. By contrast, CHIKV reactivity reported in dengue virus (DENV)- and Zika virus (ZIKV)-associated sera lacks an established biological basis and is better classified as assay-associated non-target reactivity of unresolved mechanism. These distinctions matter: unadjusted seropositivity can inflate or obscure CHIKV transmission estimates, and no single diagnostic platform resolves the problem for every virus pair. We argue that CHIKV diagnosis in co-endemic settings requires a layered strategy: molecular detection during the acute phase, antigenically informed and multiplex serology thereafter, and neutralisation-based confirmation where attribution is critical, combined with cross-reactivity-aware statistical modelling for surveillance. Strengthening assay validation and confirmatory testing, particularly in African settings such as Nigeria where CHIKV, DENV and related alphaviruses circulate together, is essential for improving diagnostic accuracy and epidemiological inference.
papers.journal: World Journal of Advanced Research and Reviews

papers.abstract_zh: 基孔肯雅病毒 (CHIKV) 会导致急性发热性疾病,并导致 关节痛 衰弱,血清学检测仍然是 诊断 和 监测 的核心。然而,在多种虫媒病毒共同循环的环境中,基于抗体的结果因交叉反应而变得复杂。本综述区分了影响 CHIKV 血清学 的三种相关但不同的现象:生物交叉反应性,由相关病毒之间真正的抗原重叠引起;与检测相关的非目标反应性,其中诊断平台在病毒之间没有建立生物学关系的情况下产生阳性信号;诊断错误分类,将两者混为一谈的下游流行病学后果。将该框架应用于五个病毒对,我们发现CHIKV-O'nyong-nyong病毒(ONNV)、CHIKV-Mayaro病毒(MAYV)和CHIKV-罗斯河病毒(RRV)关系得到了共享的甲病毒抗原结构的支持,并且在一些研究中还得到了功能性交叉中和的支持。相比之下,登革热病毒 (DENV) 和寨卡病毒 (ZIKV) 相关血清中报道的 CHIKV 反应性缺乏既定的生物学基础,最好归类为未解决机制的检测相关非靶标反应性。这些区别很重要:未经调整的血清阳性率可能会夸大或掩盖 CHIKV 传播 的估计值,并且没有一个诊断平台可以解决每个病毒对的问题。我们认为,共流行环境中的 CHIKV 诊断 需要分层策略:急性期进行分子检测,随后进行抗原告知和多重 血清学,以及基于中和的确认(其中归因至关重要),并结合 监测 的交叉反应感知统计模型。加强分析验证和确认性检测,特别是在尼日利亚等 CHIKV、DENV 和相关甲病毒共同传播的非洲地区,对于提高诊断准确性和流行病学推断至关重要。

papers.title: A MATHEMATICAL MODEL OF CHIKUNGUNYA TRANSMISSION DYNAMICS: AN APPLICATION TO DATA FROM CHAD
papers.abstract: Chikungunya is a vector-borne disease transmitted to humans by female Aedes mosquitoes, particularly Aedes albopictus. In this study, we develop a mathematical model to describe the transmission dynamics of chikungunya between humans and mosquito vectors, incorporating the effects of treatment interventions. We derive the basic reproduction number $\mathcal{R}_0$, which serves as a threshold parameter to characterize disease dynamics and establish the positivity and boundedness of solutions. Our analysis shows that the disease can be effectively controlled when $\mathcal{R}_0 < 1$. Parameter estimation is carried out using epidemiological data to inform strategies aimed at reducing secondary infections. Although no specific antiviral treatment currently exists, supportive care including the use of antibiotics for secondary infections is considered. We perform a detailed qualitative analysis of the model and conduct numerical simulations to assess the potential impact of treatment strategies and vector control measures. The results offer valuable insights into the conditions necessary for the control and possible eradication of chikungunya, particularly in the context of public health planning in affected regions such as Chad.

In this study, we develop a mathematical model to describe the transmission dynamics of chikungunya between humans and mosquito vectors, incorporating the effects of treatment interventions. We derive the basic reproduction number $\mathcal{R}_0$, which serves as a threshold parameter to characterize disease dynamics and establish the positivity and boundedness of solutions. Our analysis shows that the disease can be effectively controlled when $\mathcal{R}_0 < 1$. Parameter estimation is carried out using epidemiological data to inform strategies aimed at reducing secondary infections. Although no specific antiviral treatment currently exists, supportive care including the use of antibiotics for secondary infections is considered. We perform a detailed qualitative analysis of the model and conduct numerical simulations to assess the potential impact of treatment strategies and vector control measures. The results offer valuable insights into the conditions necessary for the control and possible eradication of chikungunya, particularly in the context of public health planning in affected regions such as Chad.
source_records.journal: Far East Journal of Mathematical Sciences (FJMS)

elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该模型应用于乍得的数据,重点关注该特定地区的疾病行为。
elements_zh.methods: 我们推导出基本再生数$\mathcal{R}_0$,它作为表征疾病动态并建立解的正性和有界性的阈值参数。使用流行病学数据进行参数估计,为旨在减少继发感染的策略提供信息。
elements_zh.main_results: 我们的分析表明,当$\mathcal{R}_0 < 1$时,疾病可以得到有效控制。研究结果为控制和可能根除基孔肯雅热所需的条件提供了宝贵的见解,特别是在乍得等受影响地区的公共卫生规划背景下。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 该研究为了解基孔肯雅热的 传播 动态提供了一个框架,并强调了 治疗 策略和 媒介 控制措施在控制该疾病方面的重要性。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果可以深入了解控制和可能根除基孔肯雅热所需的条件,从而为乍得等受影响地区的公共卫生规划提供参考。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 提供的证据没有报告该研究的具体局限性,但该模型基于流行病学数据,不包括现实世界的复杂性,例如不同的人类行为或环境因素。证据强度中等。

papers.title: Autoantibodies neutralizing type I interferons underlie a third of cases of Chikungunya virus encephalitis or myelitis
papers.abstract: Chikungunya virus (CHIKV) infection is typically not life threatening but may, in rare cases, affect the central nervous system (CNS). In three cohorts of confirmed CHIKV cases from Martinique (French overseas territory) and Brazil (patients aged 0 to 89 y, n = 245), 20 patients had CNS infection (aged 17 to 87 y). Autoantibodies neutralizing type I interferons (AAN-I-IFN) were found in 35% of patients (4 male and 3 female, aged 17 to 87 y) with encephalitis (4/15), encephalomyelitis (1/2), or myelitis (2/3), but were absent in 225 patients without CNS infection. They neutralized high concentrations (10 to 1,000 ng/mL) of IFN-α2, IFN-α8, and IFN-ω, and the antibodies of one patient also neutralized IFN-β. All samples also neutralized the other 10 IFN-α subtypes (at least 100 pg/mL). This combination of blood autoantibodies occurs in ~0.02% and 0.6% of healthy individuals under and over 70 y of age, respectively. The presence of AAN-I-IFN before CHIKV infection therefore increased the risk of CNS disease ~850-fold relative to the general population.
papers.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences

analysis.research_question_and_background: Chikungunya virus (CHIKV) infection is typically not life threatening but may, in rare cases, affect the central nervous system (CNS). This study aimed to investigate the role of autoantibodies neutralizing type I interferons in CHIKV-related CNS disease.
analysis.study_design_and_population: In three cohorts of confirmed CHIKV cases from Martinique and Brazil, 20 patients had CNS infection. Autoantibodies neutralizing type I interferons were found in 35% of patients with encephalitis, encephalomyelitis, or myelitis, but were absent in 225 patients without CNS infection.
analysis.methods: Autoantibodies neutralizing type I interferons were identified through assays that measured their ability to neutralize high concentrations of IFN-α2, IFN-α8, and IFN-ω, and the antibodies of one patient also neutralized IFN-β.
analysis.main_results: Autoantibodies neutralizing type I interferons were found in 35% of patients with CNS infection, while they were absent in 225 patients without CNS infection. They neutralized high concentrations (10 to 1,000 ng/mL) of IFN-α2, IFN-α8, and IFN-ω, and the antibodies of one patient also neutralized IFN-β.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The study found that autoantibodies neutralizing type I interferons are associated with CNS disease in CHIKV infection, suggesting a novel mechanism by which these autoantibodies may contribute to the pathogenesis of the disease.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings may inform the development of targeted diagnostic tests and therapies for CHIKV patients at risk of CNS complications, as well as improve understanding of immune mechanisms in viral infections.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its focus on specific cohorts and the potential for confounding factors, but the evidence is strong as it directly links the presence of autoantibodies to CNS disease in CHIKV patients.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the role of autoantibodies neutralizing type I interferons in Chikungunya virus (CHIKV) infections that lead to central nervous system (CNS) disease. It found that 35% of patients with CNS infection had these autoantibodies, while they were absent in 225 patients without CNS infection. The presence of these autoantibodies before CHIKV infection increased the risk of CNS disease by ~850-fold compared to the general population. The study highlights a novel mechanism involving autoantibodies in CHIKV-related CNS complications, which may have implications for diagnosis and treatment. However, the findings are based on specific cohorts and may have limitations in generalizability. The evidence is strong due to the direct association observed between autoantibodies and CNS disease.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 基孔肯雅病毒 (CHIKV) 感染通常不会危及生命,但在极少数情况下可能会影响中枢神经系统 (CNS)。本研究旨在探讨中和 I 型干扰素的自身抗体在 CHIKV 相关 CNS 疾病中的作用。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 在马提尼克岛和巴西的 3 例 队列研究 确诊 CHIKV 病例中,有 20 名患者出现中枢神经系统感染。在 35% 的脑炎、脑脊髓炎或脊髓炎患者中发现了中和 I 型干扰素的自身抗体,但在 225 名没有中枢神经系统感染的患者中则没有中和 I 型干扰素的自身抗体。
elements_zh.methods: 通过测定中和 I 型干扰素的自身抗体中和高浓度 IFN-α2、IFN-α8 和 IFN-ω 的能力,鉴定出中和 I 型干扰素的自身抗体,并且一名患者的抗体也中和了 IFN-β。

analysis_en.research_question_and_background: Chikungunya virus (CHIKV) infection is typically not life threatening but may, in rare cases, affect the central nervous system (CNS). This study aimed to investigate the role of autoantibodies neutralizing type I interferons in CHIKV-related CNS disease.
analysis_en.study_design_and_population: In three cohorts of confirmed CHIKV cases from Martinique and Brazil, 20 patients had CNS infection. Autoantibodies neutralizing type I interferons were found in 35% of patients with encephalitis, encephalomyelitis, or myelitis, but were absent in 225 patients without CNS infection.
analysis_en.methods: Autoantibodies neutralizing type I interferons were identified through assays that measured their ability to neutralize high concentrations of IFN-α2, IFN-α8, and IFN-ω, and the antibodies of one patient also neutralized IFN-β.
analysis_en.main_results: Autoantibodies neutralizing type I interferons were found in 35% of patients with CNS infection, while they were absent in 225 patients without CNS infection. They neutralized high concentrations (10 to 1,000 ng/mL) of IFN-α2, IFN-α8, and IFN-ω, and the antibodies of one patient also neutralized IFN-β.
analysis_en.interpretation_and_novelty: The study found that autoantibodies neutralizing type I interferons are associated with CNS disease in CHIKV infection, suggesting a novel mechanism by which these autoantibodies may contribute to the pathogenesis of the disease.
analysis_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings may inform the development of targeted diagnostic tests and therapies for CHIKV patients at risk of CNS complications, as well as improve understanding of immune mechanisms in viral infections.
analysis_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its focus on specific cohorts and the potential for confounding factors, but the evidence is strong as it directly links the presence of autoantibodies to CNS disease in CHIKV patients.

papers.title_zh: 三分之一的 基孔肯雅病毒 脑炎或脊髓炎病例是中和 I 型干扰素的自身抗体造成的
papers.source_body_en: Chikungunya virus (CHIKV) infection is typically not life threatening but may, in rare cases, affect the central nervous system (CNS). In three cohorts of confirmed CHIKV cases from Martinique (French overseas territory) and Brazil (patients aged 0 to 89 y, n = 245), 20 patients had CNS infection (aged 17 to 87 y). Autoantibodies neutralizing type I interferons (AAN-I-IFN) were found in 35% of patients (4 male and 3 female, aged 17 to 87 y) with encephalitis (4/15), encephalomyelitis (1/2), or myelitis (2/3), but were absent in 225 patients without CNS infection. They neutralized high concentrations (10 to 1,000 ng/mL) of IFN-α2, IFN-α8, and IFN-ω, and the antibodies of one patient also neutralized IFN-β. All samples also neutralized the other 10 IFN-α subtypes (at least 100 pg/mL). This combination of blood autoantibodies occurs in ~0.02% and 0.6% of healthy individuals under and over 70 y of age, respectively. The presence of AAN-I-IFN before CHIKV infection therefore increased the risk of CNS disease ~850-fold relative to the general population.

Case Descriptions Case 1 A 39-year-old male patient presented to the emergency department with complaints of high-grade fever associated with chills for 4 days (103.2 °F). He had associated complaints of vomiting and headache for 4 days, followed by altered sensorium for 1 day. On examination, the patient appeared disoriented and irritable, with GCS being E4V3M6. CNS examination revealed exaggerated bilateral deep tendon reflexes and a positive Babinski reflex; the remaining systemic examination was regular. The laboratory investigation revealed HIV reactive status, with the presence of antichikungunya IgM in serum and CSF (Table 1). An MRI brain Introduction Chikungunya fever (CHIKF) is an arboviral illness induced by the chikungunya virus (CHIKV), an alphavirus belonging to the Togaviridae family. Transmission occurs through a human– mosquito–human cycle initiated by a mosquito bite. Symptoms manifest after 2–6 days of incubation, characterized by high fever and intense arthralgia. The condition is self-limiting and often resolves within 2 weeks.1 Chronic illness may remain for several years, accompanied by ongoing polyarthralgia. The overlapping symptoms and shared vectors of dengue and malaria provide significant hurdles for diagnosing and treating this illness. CHIKF was initially reported in India in 1963. Following a quiescent interval of 32 years, CHIKV re-emerged in India in 2005. Every section of the nation has become endemic due to the illness, with outbreaks resulting in severe economic and production losses.1 While chikungunya is often not deemed life-threatening, unusual clinical presentations leading to considerable morbidity have been recorded, particularly during outbreaks. CHIKV infection may lead to severe sickness requiring urgent care, accompanied by considerable death. Although some fatalities are directly linked to CHIKV infection, overall mortality also rises during outbreaks.2 Chikungunya virus (CHIKV) infection is typically regarded as a benign illness regarding mortality, as severe cases are few.3,4 Recent increases in CHIKV outbreaks globally have prompted doctors and epidemiologists to focus on atypical symptoms because of their significant and occasionally lethal sequelae.5 Information about the atypical symptoms of CHIKV infection is limited, with just a few isolated case reports and hospital-based research available.6 A meticulous evaluation of the unusual symptoms is essential for comprehending the actual attributes of CHIKV infection and its 1–3Department of General Medicine, Dr DY Patil Medical College, Pune, Maharashtra, India Corresponding Author: Manaswini Edara, Department of General Medicine, Dr DY Patil Medical College, Pune, Maharashtra, India, Phone: +91 9705932453, e-mail: manaswini.edara@gmail.com How to cite this article: Raut SS, Edara M, Shivnitwar S. Source of support: Nil Conflict of interest: None Atypical Presentation of Chikungunya Virus Infection: More Than Meets the Eye Sandesh Sadanand Raut1, Manaswini Edara2, Sachin Shivnitwar3 Received on: 12 December 2024; Accepted on: 27 April 2025; Published on: 15 August 2026 Abstract Background: The recent surge in global chikungunya virus (CHIKV) outbreaks has compelled physicians and epidemiologists to concentrate on atypical symptoms because to their substantial and occasionally fatal consequences. Information regarding the unusual symptoms of CHIKV infection is scarce, with only a handful of solitary case reports and hospital-based studies accessible. A thorough assessment of the atypical symptoms is crucial for understanding the true characteristics of CHIKV infection and its effects on those afflicted. Case descriptions: Cases 1 and 2 presented with neurological manifestations, and MRI in both cases revealed nonspecific findings, which is unusual for chikungunya. Case 3 was observed to have multiple, painful, erythematous papules with hemorrhagic crusting in the bilateral groin along with tongue erosions and oral ulcers, which is often confused for sexually transmitted infections. Similarly, cases 5 and 6 presented with a maculopapular rash. Case 4 had an unusual cardiac presentation as retrosternal pain radiating to the back and bilateral lower limb edema, and she had worsening of her leprosy symptoms. Conclusion: Chikungunya viral infection can have a multitude of presentations, be it cutaneous, neurological, cardiac, or respiratory manifestations. Identifying the symptoms early can help provide timely management and improve overall outcomes. Keywords: Coryza, Lepromatous leprosy, Maculopapular rash, Viral myalgia. Case 3 A 29-year-old male patient came to the OPD with complaints of fever, high grade (102 F), which was associated with generalized weakness, myalgia, bilateral wrist tenderness, and pruritus. On examination, the patient was observed to have multiple, painful, erythematous papules with hemorrhagic crusting in the bilateral groin and well-defined erosions present over the tongue with oral ulcers. The laboratory investigation showed a platelet count of 74,000 on admission, and serum antichikungunya IgM was positive. Sexually transmitted diseases were evaluated and ruled out. The patient was treated with supportive treatments; the patient showed significant clinical improvement with healing of the lesions. On follow-up, after 4 weeks, the patient’s skin lesions were completely resolved (Fig. 3). Case 4 A 50-year-old female patient presented to the OPD with complaints of fever and vomiting for 2 days. This was associated with chest pain, retrosternal radiating to the back, and bilateral lower limb edema. She had a known case of lepromatous leprosy with type 2 lepra reaction and systemic hypertension. On examination, the patient had multiple well-defined hyperpigmented patches to papules and nodules over the bilateral upper limb, lower limb, trunk, ears, and abdomen. She also had bilateral ulnar nerve thickening, two fluid-filled bullous lesions over her right foot, along with a tender swelling of the right knee joint. The serum antichikungunya IgM was observed to be positive and associated with thrombocytopenia (79,000/mm3). Subsequently, the patient deteriorated, suspected to be in septic shock (Procalcitonin–50 ng/mL), and was started on inotropes (noradrenaline), IV meropenem 1 gm BD with oxygen support via an NRBM. The patient recovered within 3 weeks and was discharged. Case 5 An 18-year-old female patient came with a fever of 8 days, associated with chills (101 °F on admission), myalgia, arthralgia, and headache. A blanching rash and maculopapular rash on the trunk and back were noted during the examination. The patient screening was performed to confirm the diagnosis, which suggests small vessel ischemic changes (Fig. 1). The patient was treated with IV antibiotics, steroids, and IV acyclovir 500 mg TDS with added supportive care. Due to a decline in GCS, the patient was intubated and maintained on mechanical ventilation, which was started for a drop in GCS. The patient recovered after 10 days. analysis.research_question_and_background: Chikungunya virus (CHIKV) infection is often considered benign, yet atypical and severe presentations can lead to significant morbidity and mortality during outbreaks. The study aimed to examine the prevalence and frequency of atypical symptoms among patients and to ascertain demographic characteristics and concomitant diseases.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This was a case series published in the Journal of the Indian Medical Association (August 2026) examining atypical presentations of chikungunya virus infection. The study described demographic characteristics and concomitant diseases among patients presenting with atypical symptoms.
analysis.methods: The study involved detailed clinical case descriptions of patients with atypical chikungunya presentations, including neurological symptoms, laboratory investigations, and imaging where applicable. No specific laboratory methods or statistical analyses were described beyond the use of serum and CSF testing for antichikungunya IgM.
analysis.main_results: One case described a 39-year-old male with high-grade fever, vomiting, headache, and altered sensorium, with neurological examination revealing exaggerated deep tendon reflexes and a positive Babinski reflex. Laboratory findings included HIV reactive status and the presence of antichikungunya IgM in both serum and cerebrospinal fluid.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors highlight that atypical clinical presentations of CHIKV infection can lead to severe morbidity and even mortality, challenging the perception of chikungunya as a benign illness. They emphasize the need for meticulous evaluation of unusual symptoms to better understand CHIKV infection attributes.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings underscore the importance of heightened clinical vigilance for atypical chikungunya presentations, particularly in endemic regions, to prevent underdiagnosis and improve patient outcomes. This is especially relevant given the increasing global burden of CHIKV outbreaks.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence is limited to a small case series without controls or statistical analysis, which restricts generalizability and causal inference. The study relies on descriptive case reports, which may not capture the full spectrum of atypical presentations or their true prevalence.

analysis.summary_en: This case series from the Journal of the Indian Medical Association (August 2026) examined atypical presentations of chikungunya virus (CHIKV) infection, focusing on prevalence, demographic characteristics, and concomitant diseases. The study described a 39-year-old male with fever, neurological symptoms, and confirmed CHIKV infection via serum and CSF antichikungunya IgM, alongside HIV reactivity. The authors emphasize that atypical CHIKV presentations can lead to severe morbidity and mortality, challenging the view of chikungunya as a benign illness. They call for meticulous evaluation of unusual symptoms to better understand CHIKV infection. The findings highlight the need for clinical vigilance in endemic regions due to increasing global CHIKV outbreaks. However, the evidence is limited by a small, uncontrolled case series design, restricting generalizability and causal conclusions.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 基孔肯雅病毒 (CHIKV) 感染通常被认为是良性的,但非典型和严重的表现可能导致 暴发 期间的显着发病率和 死亡率。该研究旨在检查患者中的 患病率 和非典型症状的频率,并确定人口特征和伴随疾病。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 这是发表在《印度医学会杂志》(2026 年 8 月)上的一系列病例,研究了 基孔肯雅病毒 感染的非典型表现。该研究描述了出现非典型症状的患者的人口特征和伴随疾病。
elements_zh.methods: 该研究涉及非典型基孔肯雅病表现患者的详细临床病例描述,包括神经系统症状、实验室检查和适用的影像学检查。除了使用血清和脑脊液检测抗基孔肯雅 IgM 之外,没有描述具体的实验室方法或统计分析。
elements_zh.main_results: 一个病例描述了一名 39 岁男性,出现高烧、呕吐、头痛和感觉改变,神经学检查显示深部腱反射过度,巴宾斯基反射阳性。实验室检查结果包括 HIV 反应状态以及血清和脑脊液中存在抗基孔肯雅热 IgM。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者强调,CHIKV 感染的非典型临床表现可能导致严重的发病率,甚至 死亡率,挑战了基孔肯雅热作为良性疾病的看法。他们强调需要对异常症状进行仔细评估,以更好地了解 CHIKV 感染属性。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果强调了提高临床对非典型基孔肯雅病表现的警惕性的重要性,特别是在流行地区,以防止漏诊并改善患者预后。考虑到 CHIKV 暴发 日益增加的全球负担,这一点尤其重要。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 证据仅限于没有对照或统计分析的小型病例系列,这限制了普遍性和因果推理。该研究依赖于描述性 病例报告,它可能无法捕获非典型表现的全部范围或其真实的 患病率。

papers.abstract: UNLABELLED: Molecular and microscopy-based diagnostic capacity is often insufficient or unavailable in places where infectious disease burdens are highest, such as in West Africa. Rapid diagnostic testing (RDT) can provide quick and affordable diagnoses of common infections but is an imperfect solution due to limitations around detecting and dealing with false-negative and false-positive results. An alternative to RDT is unbiased metagenomic sequencing for pathogen surveillance. Here, we present data from unbiased metagenomic sequencing used to identify causes of undiagnosed febrile illness in Jos, Plateau State, Nigeria. Proof of concept for this approach has been demonstrated by several groups who have identified epidemic and endemic viral diseases like Lassa fever, yellow fever, and chikungunya. We show that unbiased deep sequencing and metagenomic analysis can be used to identify RNA viruses in clinical samples. We sequenced RNA from sera of patients (n = 343), many of whom were acutely febrile (76%), in a survey of clinics in Jos. We detected five human-infecting viruses in 39 (11 %) specimens. Among these were hepatitis B virus, human pegivirus, and several anelloviruses. While most of the viruses identified are unlikely to cause clinical symptoms in the patients we sampled, their presence demonstrates the validity of our approach. Additionally, our sequencing data allowed us to identify genetic material from potentially pathogenic bacteria, another possible etiological agent of febrile illness. IMPORTANCE: In low-resource areas, fevers due to infectious pathogens are a major source of illness, but tools for detecting and identifying such pathogens are often limited. Unbiased approaches for identifying genetic material from all potentially infectious organisms in a sample represent an opportunity for discovering sources of fever. Metagenomic sequencing can improve insight into pathogen landscapes in low-resource settings, potentially providing early detection of disease outbreaks. However, unbiased metagenomic sequencing (mNGS) is no panacea; it is susceptible to contamination and false positives. We used mNGS to evaluate serum from >300 Nigerian clinic-goers in Jos, Nigeria, most of whom (>70%) had fevers of unknown origin. Our goal was to understand arbovirus prevalence in Jos, Nigeria, and identify the sources of infection not routinely monitored for at clinics. We detected hepatitis B virus, as well as nonpathogenic anelloviruses. Our study provides insight into the utility and limitations of mNGS for pathogen surveillance.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study addresses the diagnostic gap in low-resource settings where molecular and microscopy-based tools are insufficient to identify causes of febrile illness, particularly in West Africa. It asks whether unbiased metagenomic sequencing can identify pathogens in undiagnosed febrile patients in Jos, Nigeria.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study used unbiased metagenomic sequencing on sera from 343 clinic-goers in Jos, Plateau State, Nigeria, most of whom (76%) were acutely febrile. The cohort included patients with undiagnosed febrile illness, and the samples were collected from clinics in Jos.
analysis.methods: Unbiased deep sequencing and metagenomic analysis were performed on RNA extracted from patient sera to identify RNA viruses and potentially pathogenic bacteria. The study explicitly aimed to evaluate the utility of metagenomic sequencing for pathogen surveillance in clinical samples.
analysis.main_results: The study detected five human-infecting viruses in 39 (11%) of the 343 specimens, including hepatitis B virus, human pegivirus, and several anelloviruses. While most identified viruses were unlikely to cause clinical symptoms, their presence validated the sequencing approach.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret the detection of viral and bacterial genetic material as proof of concept for metagenomic sequencing in identifying pathogens in febrile illness, demonstrating its potential for surveillance in low-resource settings. They highlight the novelty of applying unbiased sequencing to a large clinical cohort in Nigeria.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that metagenomic sequencing could improve early detection of disease outbreaks and expand pathogen surveillance in low-resource areas where diagnostic capacity is limited. This approach may inform public health strategies for managing undiagnosed febrile illness.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study acknowledges that metagenomic sequencing is susceptible to contamination and false positives, which may limit the reliability of detected pathogens. The evidence strength is moderate due to the lack of target-specific validation for clinically relevant pathogens like chikungunya virus in this dataset.

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluated unbiased metagenomic sequencing (mNGS) as a diagnostic tool for identifying pathogens in 343 febrile patients in Jos, Nigeria, where diagnostic capacity is limited. Using RNA sequencing of sera, the authors detected five human-infecting viruses in 11% of samples, including hepatitis B virus, human pegivirus, and anelloviruses, while also identifying bacterial genetic material. The approach demonstrated proof of concept for pathogen surveillance but did not detect chikungunya virus or other arboviruses targeted in the study. The authors conclude that mNGS can enhance early outbreak detection and surveillance in low-resource settings, though susceptibility to contamination and false positives limits its reliability. The evidence supports moderate confidence in the utility of mNGS for pathogen discovery but not for specific arbovirus surveillance in this cohort.

analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将病毒和细菌遗传物质的检测解释为宏基因组测序在识别发热性疾病病原体方面的概念证明,证明了 监测 在资源匮乏环境中的潜力。他们强调了将无偏测序应用于尼日利亚大型临床 队列研究 的新颖性。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明,宏基因组测序可以改善疾病 暴发 的早期检测,并在诊断能力有限的资源匮乏地区扩大病原体 暴发 的范围。这种方法可以为管理未确诊的发热性疾病的公共卫生策略提供信息。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究承认宏基因组测序容易受到污染和假阳性的影响,这可能会限制检测到的病原体的可靠性。由于该数据集中缺乏针对临床相关病原体(如 基孔肯雅病毒)的目标特异性验证,证据强度中等。

papers.title: Antibodies elicited by a chimeric peritrophin antigen reduce Aedes aegypti survival after blood feeding.
papers.abstract: Vector-borne diseases transmitted by Aedes aegypti, including dengue, Zika, chikungunya, and yellow fever, represent a persistent and expanding global health threat. Limitations of conventional vector control strategies, such as insecticide use and environmental source reduction, particularly in urban settings, underscore the need for novel and complementary tools. Anti-vector vaccination offers one such strategy by inducing host-derived antibodies that are ingested during vector feeding and interfere with vector physiology or survival. Although this concept has been successfully explored in some hematophagous arthropods, it remains largely unexplored in mosquitoes. Here, we investigated mosquito peritrophins, structural components of the midgut peritrophic matrix, as potential targets for vector-directed vaccination. We designed and recombinantly expressed a chimeric antigen, PT-3, incorporating immunogenic regions from three Aedes aegypti peritrophins/peritrophin-like proteins: AAEL002495, AAEL002467, and AAEL004798. The ability of PT-3 to elicit functional antibodies was evaluated in a bovine host model. Immunization induced a robust antigen-specific humoral response, and mosquitoes fed blood supplemented with immune sera from vaccinated animals showed significantly reduced post-feeding survival compared with controls. Consistent with this functional effect, anti-PT-3 immune sera recognized native mosquito midgut components in ELISA and Western blot assays. Overall, results are consistent with antibody-mediated interference with midgut physiological processes during blood digestion, while no significant effects on oviposition or egg viability were observed among surviving females. Together, these findings provide proof-of-concept that mosquito peritrophins can serve as immunological targets for anti-vector vaccination and provide a rationale for further developing peritrophin-targeted strategies, including alternative delivery platforms, as complementary tools for arboviral control.

elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 结果与血液消化过程中抗体介导的对中肠生理过程的干扰一致,而在幸存的雌性中没有观察到对产卵或卵子活力的显着影响。研究结果证明蚊子围营养蛋白可以作为抗 媒介 疫苗接种 的免疫靶标。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现为进一步开发围营养蛋白靶向策略(包括替代递送平台)作为虫媒病毒控制的补充工具提供了理论基础。

papers.abstract_zh: 由埃及伊蚊传播的 媒介 疾病,包括登革热、寨卡病毒、基孔肯雅热和黄热病,是一种持续且不断扩大的全球健康威胁。传统 媒介 控制策略的局限性,例如杀虫剂的使用和环境源的减少,特别是在城市环境中,强调了对新颖和补充工具的需求。抗 媒介 宿主 提供了一种这样的策略,通过诱导 宿主 衍生的抗体,这些抗体在 媒介 喂养期间摄入并干扰 媒介 生理或生存。尽管这一概念已在一些食血节肢动物中成功探索,但在蚊子中仍然很大程度上尚未探索。在这里,我们研究了蚊子围食蛋白(中肠围食基质的结构成分),作为 媒介 导向的 疫苗接种 的潜在靶标。我们设计并重组表达了嵌合抗原 PT-3,其中掺入了来自三种埃及伊蚊周营养蛋白/周营养蛋白样蛋白的免疫原性区域:AAEL002495、AAEL002467 和 AAEL004798。在牛 宿主 模型中评估了 PT-3 引发功能性抗体的能力。免疫诱导了强烈的抗原特异性体液反应,并且与对照组相比,用来自接种疫苗的动物的免疫血清喂养的蚊子的喂养后存活率显着降低。与这种功能效应一致,抗 PT-3 免疫血清在 ELISA 和蛋白质印迹测定中识别出天然蚊子中肠成分。总体而言,结果与血液消化过程中抗体介导的对中肠生理过程的干扰一致,而在幸存的雌性中没有观察到对产卵或卵子活力的显着影响。总之,这些发现提供了概念证明,即蚊子围营养蛋白可以作为抗 媒介 疫苗接种 的免疫靶点,并为进一步开发围营养蛋白靶向策略(包括替代递送平台)作为虫媒病毒控制的补充工具提供了理论基础。

papers.title: Effect of seasonal variation on the resting behavior of Aedes species (Diptera: Culicidae) in Metema district, Northwest, Ethiopia
papers.abstract: Abstract Background: Aedes mosquitoes transmit several medically important viral diseases, including dengue fever, yellow fever, chikungunya, and Zika. These diseases have re-emerged as major global public health concerns due to increasing urbanization, rising temperatures associated with climate change, and intensified human mobility. Seasonal variation, particularly between the wet and dry seasons, influences the distribution and resting behavior of Aedes species in the Metema District of northwestern Ethiopia. Method: Adult Aedes mosquitoes were collected from both indoor and outdoor resting habitats, including grain storage facilities, deep ground grooves, cattle shelters, water-holding containers, and under bridges. Collections were conducted using pyrethrum spray catches (PSC), Prokopack aspirators, and mouth aspirators. Captured mosquitoes were identified to species level under a stereomicroscope using standard morphological identification keys. Data were entered and analyzed using IBM SPSS Statistics version 20.0. Results: A total of 4,054 adult Aedes mosquitoes were collected, comprising Aedes aegypti (3,026; 74.6%), Ae. vittatus (723; 17.8%), Ae. communis (186; 4.6%), Ae. albopictus (77; 1.9%), and Ae. Significantly higher numbers of Ae. vittatus were collected from cattle shelters than from other resting habitats ( P Ae. albopictus were primarily collected from larva-positive water containers, whereas Ae. opok was predominantly collected from beneath bridges. The abundance of adult Aedes mosquitoes peaked during the wet season (June–September 2023). In contrast, during the dry season (October–May), Aedes mosquitoes were mainly found resting in deep ground grooves and beneath bridges. A high proportion of blood-fed Aedes mosquitoes was collected from cattle shelters. The predominance of Ae. vittatus in cattle shelters during the wet season is likely associated with the availability of carbon dioxide, host body heat, and protection from adverse environmental conditions. During the dry season, the resting behavior of Aedes mosquitoes shifted toward moisture-retaining habitats, such as deep ground grooves and the undersides of bridges. Conclusions These findings highlight the importance of implementing targeted Aedes mosquito control strategies that account for seasonal variation and resting habitat preferences. Particular emphasis should be placed on managing key resting sites in urban areas, especially cattle shelters during the wet season and moisture-retaining refuges during the dry season. Strengthening entomological surveillance and implementing seasonally targeted vector control interventions could substantially reduce the risk of Aedes -borne viral disease transmission in the Metema District, northwestern Ethiopia.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated seasonal variation in the resting behavior of Aedes mosquitoes in the Metema District of northwestern Ethiopia, a region where Aedes-borne viral diseases such as chikungunya are of public health concern. Adult Aedes mosquitoes were collected from multiple indoor and outdoor resting habitats using standard entomological methods and identified morphologically. A total of 4,054 adult Aedes mosquitoes were collected, with Aedes aegypti being the most abundant species (74.6%), followed by Ae. vittatus (17.8%). Significantly higher numbers of Ae. vittatus were found in cattle shelters, particularly during the wet season, while other species showed distinct habitat preferences. The abundance of adult Aedes mosquitoes peaked during the wet season, whereas during the dry season, they were mainly found in moisture-retaining habitats such as deep ground grooves and beneath bridges. The authors highlight the importance of targeted vector control strategies that account for seasonal variation and resting habitat preferences, recommending strengthened entomological surveillance and seasonally adapted interventions to reduce the risk of Aedes-borne viral disease transmission.

papers.title: Limited IgM seroreactivity to arboviruses in free-ranging black-tufted marmosets (Callithrix penicillata)
papers.abstract: Arboviruses are important causes of human disease, and several species also infect wild animals that may serve as amplifying hosts. Among these, yellow fever virus ( Orthoflavivirus flavi ) is a major cause of morbidity and mortality in neotropical primates. In addition to yellow fever virus, several other arboviruses have been reported in these animals. For example, zika virus ( Orthoflavivirus zikaense ) has been detected in free-ranging marmosets and capuchin monkeys. Antibodies against dengue virus ( Orthoflavivirus denguei ) have been identified in Alouatta spp. and Ateles spp., while Sapajus spp., Ateles marginatus , and Callithrix jacchus have been shown to develop neutralizing antibodies against chikungunya virus ( Alphavirus chikungunya ). In this study we assessed anti-arboviruses ( A. zikaense , O.Denguei , and O. flavi ) antibodies in free-ranging black-tufted marmosets ( Callithrix penicillata ) living in urban parks. Frequency of putative seroreactivity was low with 2.94% (2/68) of the captured marmosets seroreactive to A. chikungunya (IgM) and 1.47% (1/68) seroreactive to O. One marmoset was seroreactive to both viruses ( A. Arboviruses genomic sequences were not detected in serum samples, but seroreactive animals were not tested by RT-PCR due to sample limitation. This study demonstrated limited evidence of putative seroreactivity of free-ranging black-tufted marmosets to arboviruses in an area where these viruses are endemic in the human population.

analysis.research_question_and_background: This study aimed to assess the seroreactivity of free-ranging black-tufted marmosets to arboviruses, particularly in an area where these viruses are endemic in humans. Arboviruses are important causes of human disease, and several species also infect wild animals that may serve as amplifying hosts.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study was conducted in urban parks where free-ranging black-tufted marmosets (Callithrix penicillata) reside. A total of 68 marmosets were captured and tested for seroreactivity to arboviruses, including chikungunya virus, in an area where these viruses are endemic in the human population.
analysis.methods: Seroreactivity to arboviruses was assessed using antibody detection methods. Arboviruses genomic sequences were not detected in serum samples, but seroreactive animals were not tested by RT-PCR due to sample limitation.
analysis.main_results: The frequency of putative seroreactivity was low, with 2.94% (2/68) of the captured marmosets seroreactive to chikungunya virus (IgM) and 1.47% (1/68) seroreactive to dengue virus. One marmoset was seroreactive to both viruses.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The study demonstrated limited evidence of putative seroreactivity of free-ranging black-tufted marmosets to arboviruses, highlighting the need for further investigation into the role of these animals in arbovirus transmission.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that free-ranging black-tufted marmosets may not be significant amplifying hosts for chikungunya virus, which has implications for understanding the ecology and transmission dynamics of arboviruses in urban settings.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study had limited sample size and did not test seroreactive animals by RT-PCR due to sample constraints, which may affect the strength of the evidence. The confidence in the findings is moderate due to these limitations.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the seroreactivity of free-ranging black-tufted marmosets to arboviruses, particularly chikungunya virus, in an urban area where these viruses are endemic in humans. The research aimed to understand the potential role of these primates in arbovirus transmission. Results showed low seroreactivity rates, with 2.94% of marmosets reactive to chikungunya virus (IgM) and 1.47% to dengue virus. One marmoset was found to be seroreactive to both viruses. The study highlights the limited evidence of seroreactivity in these animals, suggesting they may not be significant amplifying hosts for arboviruses. However, the findings are limited by the small sample size and lack of RT-PCR testing for seroreactive individuals, resulting in moderate confidence in the conclusions.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 这项研究旨在评估自由放养的黑簇绒狨猴对虫媒病毒的血清反应性,特别是在这些病毒在人类中流行的地区。虫媒病毒是人类疾病的重要原因,一些物种也感染野生动物,这些动物可能起到放大 宿主 的作用。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 这项研究是在城市公园进行的,那里栖息着自由放养的黑簇绒狨猴(Callithrix penicillata)。在这些病毒在人群中流行的地区,总共捕获了 68 只狨猴并测试了其对虫媒病毒(包括 基孔肯雅病毒)的血清反应性。
elements_zh.methods: 使用抗体检测方法评估对虫媒病毒的血清反应性。血清样本中未检测到虫媒病毒基因组序列,但由于样本限制,未对血清反应性动物进行 RT-PCR 检测。
elements_zh.main_results: 假定的血清反应频率较低,捕获的狨猴中有 2.94% (2/68) 对 基孔肯雅病毒 (IgM) 有血清反应,对登革热病毒有 1.47% (1/68) 血清反应。一只狨猴对这两种病毒均呈血清反应。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 该研究证明,自由放养的黑簇绒狨猴对虫媒病毒具有血清反应性的证据有限,强调需要进一步研究这些动物在虫媒病毒 传播 中的作用。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明,自由放养的黑簇绒狨猴可能不会显着放大 宿主 的 基孔肯雅病毒,这对于了解城市环境中虫媒病毒的生态和 传播 动态具有重要意义。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究样本量有限,由于样本限制,没有通过RT-PCR测试血清反应动物,这可能会影响证据的强度。由于这些限制,研究结果的可信度较低。

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 这项研究旨在评估自由放养的黑簇绒狨猴对虫媒病毒的血清反应性,特别是在这些病毒在人类中流行的地区。虫媒病毒是人类疾病的重要原因,一些物种也感染野生动物,这些动物可能起到放大 宿主 的作用。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 这项研究是在城市公园进行的,那里栖息着自由放养的黑簇绒狨猴(Callithrix penicillata)。在这些病毒在人群中流行的地区,总共捕获了 68 只狨猴并测试了其对虫媒病毒(包括 基孔肯雅病毒)的血清反应性。
analysis_zh.methods: 使用抗体检测方法评估对虫媒病毒的血清反应性。血清样本中未检测到虫媒病毒基因组序列,但由于样本限制,未对血清反应性动物进行 RT-PCR 检测。
analysis_zh.main_results: 假定的血清反应频率较低,捕获的狨猴中有 2.94% (2/68) 对 基孔肯雅病毒 (IgM) 有血清反应,对登革热病毒有 1.47% (1/68) 血清反应。一只狨猴对这两种病毒均呈血清反应。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 该研究证明,自由放养的黑簇绒狨猴对虫媒病毒具有血清反应性的证据有限,强调需要进一步研究这些动物在虫媒病毒 传播 中的作用。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明,自由放养的黑簇绒狨猴可能不会显着放大 宿主 的 基孔肯雅病毒,这对于了解城市环境中虫媒病毒的生态和 传播 动态具有重要意义。

papers.title: Indirect Immunofluorescence (IFA) for Viral Antigen Detection v1
papers.abstract: A protocol for indirect immunofluorescence assay (IFA) to detect viral antigens in infected cell monolayers or tissue sections using virus-specific primary antibodies and fluorochrome-conjugated secondary antibodies. Covers cell infection, fixation, permeabilization, antibody staining, and fluorescence microscopy imaging. Protocol developed by abinScience / AtaGenix Technical Team. Indirect immunofluorescence (IFA) is a standard method for confirming viral infection, determining viral tropism, and evaluating antiviral interventions in cell culture. The assay uses a virus-specific primary antibody to bind intracellular or surface viral antigens, followed by a fluorochrome-conjugated secondary antibody for visualization. This protocol is optimized for common veterinary and human pathogen targets including PEDV (porcine epidemic diarrhea virus), SFTSV (severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome virus), CHIKV (chikungunya virus), ASFV (African swine fever virus), and other enveloped and non-enveloped viruses. It is applicable to both adherent and suspension cell lines.

analysis.summary_en: This preprint describes an indirect immunofluorescence (IFA) assay for detecting viral antigens in infected cell monolayers or tissue sections. The method employs virus‐specific primary antibodies that bind intracellular or surface viral antigens and a fluorochrome‐conjugated secondary antibody for visualization, and includes steps such as cell infection, fixation, permeabilization, staining, and fluorescence microscopy imaging of both adherent and suspension cell lines. The protocol is optimized for several veterinary and human pathogens, including Chikungunya virus, and is presented as a standard tool for confirming viral infection, determining viral tropism, and evaluating antiviral interventions in cell culture. No quantitative results or outcome data are provided in the supplied evidence, and the manuscript offers no explicit discussion of study limitations or evidence strength. Consequently, the work serves as a methodological reference for CHIKV detection and related applications, highlighting the assay’s broad utility across enveloped and non‐enveloped viruses.

papers.title: Etiological Spectrum of Acute Febrile Illness in a Tertiary Care Hospital in Assam, India: A Cross-Sectional Study
papers.abstract: Introduction: Acute Febrile Illness (AFI) encompasses a spectrum of conditions marked by fever, often caused by various infectious agents. The aetiological diversity poses challenges in diagnosis and treatment, particularly in regions with limited diagnostic resources. Aim: To evaluate the spectrum of pathogens causing AFI with or without rash in patients. Materials and Methods: A hospital-based cross-sectional study was conducted from January 2024 to December 2024 on 1,544 patients who had attended Lakhimpur Medical College and Hospital, North Lakhimpur, Assam, India. Patients with fever (≥ 37.5°C) with or without rash were enrolled. Serological investigations for Measles, Rubella, Dengue, Varicella-zoster, Chikungunya viruses, Japanese Encephalitis (JE), Orientia tsutsugamushi, Leptospira, and Hepatitis viruses were performed using Enzyme-linked Immunosorbent assay (ELISA) and Rapid Detection Testing (RDT) kits. Data analysis was performed using both descriptive and inferential methods. A p-value of <0.05 was considered significant. Results: Fever was prevalent in all 1,544 (100%) cases, followed by 856 (55.44%) cases of headache, 636 (41.19%) with cough, 476 (30.83%) with vomiting, 347 (22.47%) with abdominal pain, 59 (3.82%) cases with dysentery, 52 (3.37%) with diarrhoea, 46 (2.98%) cases with unconsciousness, and 21 (1.36%) cases presented with rash. Fever was observed in combination with headache in 856 (55.44%), with cough in 636 (41.19%), with bodyache in 481 (31.15%), and with vomiting in 476 (30.83%) cases. The study identified seasonal variations in infection rates, with peaks during the monsoon months. The majority of positive cases were attributed to Scrub Typhus 133/817 (16.28%), followed by Leptospirosis 129/473 (27.27%), Dengue 84/1273 (6.59%), and JE 20/87 (22.99%), while some had co-infection. Conclusion: The study underscores the importance of integrated clinical and laboratory approaches in diagnosing AFI. Scrub typhus, leptospirosis, and dengue were identified as major causes, emphasising the need for enhanced surveillance and diagnostic capabilities.

Aim: To evaluate the spectrum of pathogens causing AFI with or without rash in patients. Materials and Methods: A hospital-based cross-sectional study was conducted from January 2024 to December 2024 on 1,544 patients who had attended Lakhimpur Medical College and Hospital, North Lakhimpur, Assam, India. Patients with fever (≥ 37.5°C) with or without rash were enrolled. Serological investigations for Measles, Rubella, Dengue, Varicella-zoster, Chikungunya viruses, Japanese Encephalitis (JE), Orientia tsutsugamushi, Leptospira, and Hepatitis viruses were performed using Enzyme-linked Immunosorbent assay (ELISA) and Rapid Detection Testing (RDT) kits. Data analysis was performed using both descriptive and inferential methods. A p-value of <0.05 was considered significant. Results: Fever was prevalent in all 1,544 (100%) cases, followed by 856 (55.44%) cases of headache, 636 (41.19%) with cough, 476 (30.83%) with vomiting, 347 (22.47%) with abdominal pain, 59 (3.82%) cases with dysentery, 52 (3.37%) with diarrhoea, 46 (2.98%) cases with unconsciousness, and 21 (1.36%) cases presented with rash. Fever was observed in combination with headache in 856 (55.44%), with cough in 636 (41.19%), with bodyache in 481 (31.15%), and with vomiting in 476 (30.83%) cases. The study identified seasonal variations in infection rates, with peaks during the monsoon months. The majority of positive cases were attributed to Scrub Typhus 133/817 (16.28%), followed by Leptospirosis 129/473 (27.27%), Dengue 84/1273 (6.59%), and JE 20/87 (22.99%), while some had co-infection. Conclusion: The study underscores the importance of integrated clinical and laboratory approaches in diagnosing AFI. Scrub typhus, leptospirosis, and dengue were identified as major causes, emphasising the need for enhanced surveillance and diagnostic capabilities.

analysis.summary_en: This cross-sectional study conducted in a tertiary care hospital in Assam, India, from January to December 2024 aimed to evaluate the spectrum of pathogens causing Acute Febrile Illness (AFI) with or without rash. The study identified fever as the most prevalent symptom, with seasonal variations noted. While the study found that Scrub Typhus, Leptospirosis, and Dengue were major causes, it emphasized the need for integrated clinical and laboratory approaches for accurate diagnosis. The findings suggest the importance of enhanced surveillance and diagnostic capabilities in resource-limited settings. However, the study's limitations include its focus on a single hospital, which may affect generalizability, and its reliance on serological testing, which may not capture all pathogens. The evidence is of moderate strength due to the observational design.

elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 2024 年 1 月至 2024 年 12 月期间,对印度阿萨姆邦北拉金布尔拉金布尔医学院和医院就诊的 1,544 名患者进行了一项以医院为基础的横断面研究。发热(≥ 37.5°C)伴或不伴皮疹的患者纳入研究。

elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 该研究强调了综合临床和实验室方法在诊断 AFI 中的重要性。恙虫病、钩端螺旋体病和登革热被确定为主要原因,强调需要增强 监测 和诊断能力。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果强调了改进诊断工具和 监测 系统的必要性,以解决 AFI 的多种病因,特别是在资源有限的环境中。感染率的季节性变化可以为预防和控制的公共卫生策略提供信息。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究仅限于印度阿萨姆邦的一家三级护理医院,可能无法推广到其他地区。该证据基于血清学检测,并且由于该研究的观察性质而具有中等强度。

papers.title: OVERVIEW OF THE MOST FREQUENTLY OCCURRING NOTIFIABLE INFECTIOUS DISEASES IN AMAZONAS BETWEEN 2021 AND 2025
papers.abstract: Introduction: Compulsory notification is the mandatory reporting of suspected or confirmed diseases, health conditions, or public health events by healthcare professionals and services to health authorities. Objective: To describe the epidemiological profile of major infectious diseases (endemic diseases, arboviruses, respiratory viral infections, and emerging or re-emerging notifiable diseases) in Amazonas. Methodology: This is a retrospective descriptive study using a quantitative approach to public data to present descriptive statistics and temporal trends. Only data obtained directly from epidemiological bulletins published on the website of the Amazonas Health Surveillance Foundation (FVS-RCP) for the years 2021 to 2025 were included. Results: During this period, 391,189 cases of infections considered most recurrent in Amazonas were reported. The majority of cases (332,019; 84.9%) involved infectious diseases of major epidemiological importance, including endemic conditions: malaria, tuberculosis, leishmaniasis, leprosy, viral hepatitis, and syphilis in infants under one year of age. Regarding dengue—considered the most frequent arbovirus in the state—there were 31,402 (8.03%) cases during the period. For Chikungunya, Zika, Oropouche, and Mayaro—arboviruses requiring immediate notification but occurring less frequently—there were 1,336 (0.3%) cases. A significant number of respiratory infections caused by Influenza viruses and COVID-19 (16,874; 4.3%) were also recorded. Significant fluctuations and spikes in the incidence of these infectious diseases were observed in Amazonas between 2021 and 2025. papers.title: Evidence of co-circulation and co-exposure to arboviruses and malaria in a longitudinal cohort in Kenya from 2019 to 2022
papers.abstract: Chikungunya virus (CHIKV), dengue virus (DENV), and malaria have gained significant concern in sub-Saharan Africa. The similar epidemiology, endemicity and clinical presentation of the diseases caused by these pathogens underscore the need to investigate the burden and emergence of mixed infections and the potential factors that increase the risk of coexistence and co-circulation of these pathogens. In this study, we determine the burden of co-exposure and co-infection of CHIKV, DENV, and malaria in Kenya and describe the associated risk factors. We followed 4,534 study participants from December 2019 to February 2022 on the coast (Ukunda) and west (Kisumu) of Kenya to quantify the burden of CHIKV, DENV, and malaria co-infections and recent and lifetime co-exposure. The results highlight 15.5% acute malarial infection, 0.7% acute DENV infection, and 0.06% acute CHIKV infection in our cohort. No acute co-infection was detected. The lifetime co-exposure to DENV and malaria was 0.75% and CHIKV and malaria was 1.8%. We estimated ~ 0.2% of the study population to be co-exposed to DENV, CHIKV, and malaria. The study highlights the importance of higher socioeconomic status, mosquito prevention methods, and sleeping under the bed nets to decrease the co-exposure to DENV, CHIKV, and malaria and, crowding and presence of water containers to increase the co-exposure to DENV, CHIKV, and malaria.

The similar epidemiology, endemicity and clinical presentation of the diseases caused by these pathogens underscore the need to investigate the burden and emergence of mixed infections and the potential factors that increase the risk of coexistence and co-circulation of these pathogens. In this study, we determine the burden of co-exposure and co-infection of CHIKV, DENV, and malaria in Kenya and describe the associated risk factors. We followed 4,534 study participants from December 2019 to February 2022 on the coast (Ukunda) and west (Kisumu) of Kenya to quantify the burden of CHIKV, DENV, and malaria co-infections and recent and lifetime co-exposure. The results highlight 15.5% acute malarial infection, 0.7% acute DENV infection, and 0.06% acute CHIKV infection in our cohort. No acute co-infection was detected. The lifetime co-exposure to DENV and malaria was 0.75% and CHIKV and malaria was 1.8%. We estimated ~ 0.2% of the study population to be co-exposed to DENV, CHIKV, and malaria. The study highlights the importance of higher socioeconomic status, mosquito prevention methods, and sleeping under the bed nets to decrease the co-exposure to DENV, CHIKV, and malaria and, crowding and presence of water containers to increase the co-exposure to DENV, CHIKV, and malaria.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study addresses the growing public-health concern posed by chikungunya virus (CHIKV), dengue virus (DENV), and malaria in sub-Saharan Africa, where similar clinical presentations complicate diagnosis and control. It asks whether these pathogens co-circulate and co-expose individuals, and what risk factors drive their coexistence.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A longitudinal cohort study followed 4,534 participants from December 2019 to February 2022 in two Kenyan sites: Ukunda on the coast and Kisumu in the west. The design aimed to quantify the burden of co-infections and co-exposures to CHIKV, DENV, and malaria.
analysis.methods: The study measured acute infections and lifetime co-exposure to CHIKV, DENV, and malaria using serological and parasitological assays in a defined cohort over a 27-month period.
analysis.main_results: Acute malarial infection was detected in 15.5% of participants, acute DENV in 0.7%, and acute CHIKV in 0.06%. No acute co-infections were detected, while lifetime co-exposure to DENV and malaria was 0.75%, to CHIKV and malaria was 1.8%, and to all three pathogens was estimated at ~0.2%.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret the low prevalence of acute CHIKV and the absence of acute co-infections as evidence of limited immediate clinical overlap, while highlighting measurable lifetime co-exposure that may inform future surveillance strategies.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that socioeconomic factors, mosquito prevention, and bed-net use may reduce co-exposure risk, whereas crowding and water containers may increase it, guiding targeted interventions in endemic regions.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study’s abstract-only evidence and lack of detailed methods or statistical power assessments limit the strength of conclusions; further data are needed to confirm risk factors and generalisability.

analysis.summary_en: This longitudinal cohort study in Kenya quantified the burden of co-exposure and co-infection to chikungunya virus (CHIKV), dengue virus (DENV), and malaria among 4,534 participants from December 2019 to February 2022. Acute infections were detected in 15.5% for malaria, 0.7% for DENV, and 0.06% for CHIKV, with no acute co-infections observed. Lifetime co-exposure was 0.75% for DENV and malaria, 1.8% for CHIKV and malaria, and ~0.2% for all three pathogens. The authors link higher socioeconomic status, mosquito prevention, and bed-net use to reduced co-exposure risk, while crowding and water containers may increase it. However, the abstract-only evidence and absence of detailed methods limit the strength of these conclusions.

papers.title: RNA Cis-Elements Involved in Animal Virus Stop Codon Readthrough: Stop Codon Context and Downstream RNA Structures
papers.abstract: Stop codon readthrough is a noncanonical translation strategy employed by certain RNA viruses, in which a viral termination codon is either decoded by host near-cognate tRNAs or canonically recognized by the class I release factor (RF, eRF1 in eukaryotes). Ribosomal A-site competition between near-cognate tRNAs and eRF can shift decoding toward near-cognate tRNAs, thereby promoting non-canonical decoding events by transiently pausing termination and favoring readthrough. This review focuses on two viral cis-elements that modulate readthrough across four viral genera in which this decoding event has been experimentally validated: (i) primary sequences surrounding the stop codon (stop codon context), and (ii) downstream RNA structures. Effects of stop codon context have been observed more broadly in cellular genes, including nonsense suppression in bacteria, with mechanisms including inefficient RF association or tRNA interactions at adjacent sense codons. In eukaryotic systems, interactions with the ribosomal mRNA entry channel have been suggested. Diverse downstream structures, including gammaretroviral pseudoknots and specific structures in alpha- and coltiviruses, further stimulate readthrough in a location- and structure-sensitive manner. This effect has not been consistently observed in chikungunya and triatoviral structures, suggesting a strong dependence on local sequence and structural context. Compared with the larger number of cellular readthrough occurrences that can be detected at low efficiency by ribosome profiling, viral readthrough in mammalian systems is consistently high (>2%). Understanding the interplay between viral RNA elements and host translational machinery, including potential kinetic trapping at the termination codon, provides insights into this unusual elongation mechanism. These findings may have implications for antiviral strategies targeting these RNA elements.

analysis.summary_en: This review explores the mechanisms of stop codon readthrough in Chikungunya virus, focusing on cis-elements that modulate this process. It highlights the role of stop codon context and downstream RNA structures in promoting readthrough, which is a noncanonical translation strategy. The review notes that while stop codon readthrough is common in cellular genes, its occurrence in viral systems, particularly in Chikungunya virus, is more consistent and significant. It also discusses the potential implications of these findings for antiviral strategies. However, the effect of stop codon context on readthrough is not consistently observed in all viral genera, indicating a strong dependence on local sequence and structural context. The review emphasizes the importance of understanding the interaction between viral RNA elements and host translational machinery to develop targeted interventions.

papers.title_zh: 参与动物病毒终止密码子通读的 RNA 顺式元件:终止密码子背景和下游 RNA 结构
papers.source_body_en: Stop codon readthrough is a noncanonical translation strategy employed by certain RNA viruses, in which a viral termination codon is either decoded by host near-cognate tRNAs or canonically recognized by the class I release factor (RF, eRF1 in eukaryotes). Ribosomal A-site competition between near-cognate tRNAs and eRF can shift decoding toward near-cognate tRNAs, thereby promoting non-canonical decoding events by transiently pausing termination and favoring readthrough. This review focuses on two viral cis-elements that modulate readthrough across four viral genera in which this decoding event has been experimentally validated: (i) primary sequences surrounding the stop codon (stop codon context), and (ii) downstream RNA structures. Effects of stop codon context have been observed more broadly in cellular genes, including nonsense suppression in bacteria, with mechanisms including inefficient RF association or tRNA interactions at adjacent sense codons. In eukaryotic systems, interactions with the ribosomal mRNA entry channel have been suggested. Diverse downstream structures, including gammaretroviral pseudoknots and specific structures in alpha- and coltiviruses, further stimulate readthrough in a location- and structure-sensitive manner. This effect has not been consistently observed in chikungunya and triatoviral structures, suggesting a strong dependence on local sequence and structural context. Compared with the larger number of cellular readthrough occurrences that can be detected at low efficiency by ribosome profiling, viral readthrough in mammalian systems is consistently high (>2%). Understanding the interplay between viral RNA elements and host translational machinery, including potential kinetic trapping at the termination codon, provides insights into this unusual elongation mechanism. These findings may have implications for antiviral strategies targeting these RNA elements.
papers.abstract_zh: 终止密码子通读是某些 RNA 病毒采用的非规范翻译策略,其中病毒终止密码子要么由 宿主 近同源 tRNA 解码,要么由 I 类释放因子(真核生物中的 RF、eRF1)规范识别。近同源 tRNA 和 eRF 之间的核糖体 A 位点竞争可以将解码转向近同源 tRNA,从而通过短暂暂停终止和有利于通读来促进非规范解码事件。本综述重点关注两个病毒顺式元件,它们调节四个病毒属的通读,其中该解码事件已通过实验验证:(i) 终止密码子周围的一级序列(终止密码子上下文),以及 (ii) 下游 RNA 结构。终止密码子环境的影响在细胞基因中得到了更广泛的观察,包括细菌中的无义抑制,其机制包括低效的 RF 关联或相邻有义密码子处的 tRNA 相互作用。在真核系统中,已提出与核糖体 mRNA 进入通道的相互作用。不同的下游结构,包括γ逆转录病毒假结以及α病毒和大肠杆菌病毒中的特定结构,以位置和结构敏感的方式进一步刺激通读。在基孔肯雅热和三核病毒结构中尚未一致地观察到这种效应,表明对局部序列和结构背景的强烈依赖性。与通过核糖体分析以低效率检测到的大量细胞通读发生相比,哺乳动物系统中的病毒通读始终很高(>2%)。了解病毒 RNA 元件和 宿主 翻译机制之间的相互作用,包括终止密码子处的潜在动力学捕获,可以深入了解这种不寻常的延伸机制。这些发现可能对针对这些 RNA 元件的 抗病毒药物 策略产生影响。
